issues.legal_issue: A High Court may exercise revisional jurisdiction under the Code of Civil Procedure over a District Judge’s revisional order under the rent-control statute, even though that statute describes the District Judge’s order as final.
material_facts: A District Judge made an order while exercising revisional jurisdiction under the rent-control statute.
The High Court dismissed a further revision as not maintainable, relying on a later Full Bench decision that had treated the earlier Full Bench decision as no longer good law.
The statutory provision made the District Judge’s order final but contained no express words removing the High Court’s revisional jurisdiction under the Code of Civil Procedure.
The Supreme Court had previously decided that a revision under the Code of Civil Procedure was available against an order under the same statutory provision.
issues.conclusion: A revision application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 50(1) of the Karnataka Rent Control Act is maintainable against a District Judge’s revisional order under section 50(2).
issues.legal_principle: Under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court may revise orders of subordinate courts, subject to that section’s limitations. The description of an order as final does not, without express statutory words excluding the jurisdiction, remove that power. Chhagan Lal v. Municipal Corporation, Indore and Krishnadas Bhatija v. A.S. Venkatachala Shetty support the availability of revision; Krishnaji Venkatesh Shirodkar v. Gurupad Shivaram Kavalekar was approved. Vishesh Kumar v. Shanti Prasad and Aundal Ammal v. Sadasivan Pillai were distinguished because they concerned different statutory schemes.

rule.if: rent_control_revision_case and district_judge_made_revisional_order and district_judge_order_called_final and no_express_exclusion_of_high_court_revision

predicates.rent_control_revision_case: The proceeding concerns a revision under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.district_judge_made_revisional_order: A District Judge made the challenged order while exercising revisional jurisdiction.
predicates.district_judge_order_called_final: The governing scheme describes the District Judge’s order as final.
predicates.no_express_exclusion_of_high_court_revis: The governing scheme contains no express words removing the High Court’s power to revise the District Judge’s order.

issues.definition: When a rent-control revision produces a District Judge’s order described as final, but the scheme does not expressly exclude further High Court revision, the High Court revision is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A coordinate High Court bench may not treat an earlier Full Bench decision as overruled when that decision has not been directly overruled by the Supreme Court or rendered unsustainable by necessary implication.
material_facts: An earlier Full Bench of the High Court had held that the High Court could revise a District Judge’s order under the rent-control statute.
That Full Bench relied on a Supreme Court decision and on a later Supreme Court decision addressing the same statutory provision.
A later Full Bench held that the earlier decision no longer survived, relying on Supreme Court decisions concerning different statutory schemes.
The Supreme Court had not directly overruled the earlier Full Bench decision, and the later decisions did not make its reasoning unsustainable by necessary implication.
issues.conclusion: The earlier Full Bench decision remained binding, and the coordinate Full Bench should not have treated it as overruled.
issues.legal_principle: A Full Bench decision binds a bench of equal strength unless the Supreme Court directly overrules it or it becomes unsustainable by necessary implication. Article 141 of the Constitution makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts, and judicial propriety requires lower courts to follow decisions of superior courts. The Court referred to Broom v. Cassell & Co. and approved the principle that each lower tier must loyally accept decisions of higher tiers.

rule.if: appeal_from_revision_dismissal and earlier_full_bench_decided_same_issue and earlier_full_bench_supported_by_supreme_court_authority and later_decisions_addressed_different_statutory_schemes and no_direct_or_necessary_supreme_court_overruling

predicates.appeal_from_revision_dismissal: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision dismissing a revision as not maintainable.
predicates.earlier_full_bench_decided_same_issue: An earlier Full Bench of the same High Court decided the issue now in dispute.
predicates.earlier_full_bench_supported_by_supreme_: The earlier Full Bench based its decision on authority of the Supreme Court.
predicates.later_decisions_addressed_different_stat: The later Supreme Court decisions relied on to displace the earlier decision concerned different statutory schemes.
predicates.no_direct_or_necessary_supreme_court_ove: The Supreme Court has neither directly overruled the earlier decision nor made it unsustainable by necessary implication.

issues.definition: When an earlier Full Bench decided the same issue on Supreme Court authority, later decisions concern different statutory schemes, and the Supreme Court has not directly or necessarily displaced the earlier ruling, that ruling remains binding.
